clue.text: Lady finding singles in pubs

indicators.note: the singles are placed in the pubs, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: bars are pubs
singles are ones, single units

explanation.surface: A woman picks up unattached partners while doing the rounds of the local pubs.
explanation.definitionFit: A noblewoman holding that rank is addressed as Lady, so the title fits as a synonym.

clue.text: Rifle is also left raised

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising the letters means reading them from bottom to top

parts.note: too means also

explanation.surface: A gun has been propped up on its left side, too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rifle' looks like a noun, the gun, but it is a verb: to ransack.
explanation.definitionFit: To rifle a place is to search through it and steal, a synonym of plundering it.

clue.text: Get the next round in!

parts.note: reads as a call at the bar for more drinks, but a round is also a cartridge put into a gun

explanation.surface: Someone at the pub urges a friend to buy the next drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: A round of drinks misleads; a round of ammunition is what goes back into the weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting a fresh cartridge into a gun after firing means charging it again with ammunition.

clue.text: Search bank becoming poorer

parts.note: to scan is to search
a bank is a row or tier, as of seats or oars

explanation.surface: An investigation into a bank leaves it worse off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' suggests money; here it is a row, as in a bank of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: Something scantier is more meagre, less plentiful, so it is poorer in amount.

clue.text: Chopped hot recipe holding large chopper …

indicators.note: the rearranged letters hold the next piece within them
chopping the words cuts them up so their letters can be rearranged

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing sizes

explanation.surface: A cookery instruction to chop up a spicy dish, with a big chopping knife, leading into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chopped' rearranges HOT RECIPE, and 'holding' puts L inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Chopper is informal slang for a rotor aircraft, from the chopping sound of its blades.

clue.text: … hot dish is cold, it's said

indicators.note: this signals that the word for cold is spoken, giving a different spelling

parts.note: chilly means cold

explanation.surface: Continuing the kitchen theme: a spicy meal is served cold, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links it to the previous clue but adds nothing to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Chilli con carne is a spicy stew, often just called by its pepper's name, so a hot dish.

clue.text: General French refusal to arrest a European …

indicators.note: arresting someone holds them, so the refusal holds the next pieces inside it

parts.note: non is French for no
a Pole is a European

explanation.surface: A French general refuses to have a fellow European detained.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon Bonaparte was the famous French military commander, a general before becoming emperor.

clue.text: Mesh covers the woman's bottom!

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece covering another sits on top of it, so it comes first

parts.note: net is a mesh
her means belonging to the woman

explanation.surface: A cheeky line about a woman wearing fishnet over her behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottom' reads as a noun, a backside, but is the adjective meaning lowest.
explanation.definitionFit: Nether means lower or lowest, as in the nether regions, so bottom used as an adjective.

clue.text: … reportedly arrests Europeans

indicators.note: signals that the word meaning arrests is heard rather than read

parts.note: checks means halts or arrests, as in checking progress

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: it is said that the police detain people from Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrests' suggests police; here it means halts.
explanation.definitionFit: People from the Czech Republic are Europeans, an example of the broader category.

clue.text: Fool could make love in bed

indicators.note: love is placed in the bed

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: An idiot could be romantic in the bedroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make love' is a red herring: 'could make' is a link and love is the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: An old coot is informal for a foolish or eccentric person, especially an elderly one.

clue.text: Seeming old and wise taking time

indicators.note: the old and wise pieces take in the time letter

parts.note: sensible means wise

explanation.surface: A sage elder appears thoughtful while taking their time.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostensible describes what is apparent on the surface, a synonym of seeming or apparent.

clue.text: Slow blast with Queen in comeback

indicators.note: coming back means the letters are read in reverse order

parts.note: drat and blast are both mild curses
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: A sluggish explosion as the Queen makes a return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blast' is the exclamation, not an explosion.
explanation.definitionFit: To retard something is to delay or hold it back, a verb synonym of slow.

clue.text: Terrible meal in tray is nourishing

indicators.note: a terrible state of the words means they are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: An awful hospital meal on a tray is still healthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Alimentary relates to food and nutrition, as in alimentary canal, so it means nourishing.

clue.text: Occasional record with one disco dancing

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: dancing words are jumbled about into a new order

explanation.surface: A record played now and then while dancing at a disco.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' rearranges DISCO into SODIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Episodic means happening in separate episodes at intervals, so occasional or sporadic.

clue.text: Cuts back almost everything getting wind

indicators.note: back means the word for cuts is read backwards

parts.note: rips are cuts or tears

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: all means everything

explanation.surface: Budget cuts are reversed while nearly everybody picks up a breeze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses RIPS to SPIR; 'almost' trims ALL to AL. 'wind' is a verb, to coil, not the breeze.
explanation.definitionFit: To spiral is to wind or coil around in a curve, a verb synonym.

clue.text: 'Surprise!', like host in broadcast

parts.note: as means like

indicators.note: broadcast seed is scattered, so the letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A television presenter shouts a surprise during a broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' scatters HOST IN to give TONISH.
explanation.definitionFit: To astonish someone is to amaze or surprise them greatly, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Hollow and irritated about Republican

indicators.note: the irritated phrase goes about, around, the Republican letter

parts.note: got to means irritated, as in it really got to me

explanation.surface: An empty-feeling politician is annoyed by a Republican.
explanation.walkthrough: 'irritated' is the phrase GOT TO, as in 'that remark got to me'.
explanation.definitionFit: A grotto is a small cave, a hollow in rock.

clue.text: Lover castigated about being dull

indicators.note: the letters are found about, within, the run of words that follow on

explanation.surface: A sweetheart is told off for being boring.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit inside 'Lover castigated', dropping the opening L and the closing IGATED.
explanation.definitionFit: An overcast sky is clouded over and grey, so a dull day.

clue.text: Sailors consumed by ship's propellers

indicators.note: the sailors are swallowed inside the ship's letters

parts.note: SS is a steamship, a ship's prefix
the crew are the sailors aboard

explanation.surface: Sailors get eaten up by a vessel's engines.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's screws are its propellers, the screw-shaped blades that drive it.

clue.text: Liberal vote for keeping Conservative in charge

indicators.note: the vote keeps the next letter inside it

parts.note: to elect is to vote in

explanation.surface: A Liberal votes to keep the Conservatives in power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liberal' looks like the party, but means broad in taste.
explanation.definitionFit: Eclectic taste draws widely from many sources, so it is broad, liberal or open.

clue.text: Anger from sticky situation trapped by credit

indicators.note: the sticky situation is trapped inside the credit letters

parts.note: being in a hole is being in a sticky situation

explanation.surface: Fury at being caught in a financial mess by one's lender.
explanation.definitionFit: Choler is an old word for irritability or rage, one of the four humours.

clue.text: Modicum of egotism or selfishness

indicators.note: of signals the letters come out of the run of words that follow

explanation.surface: A trace of vanity or self-interest.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'egotisM OR SELfishness'.
explanation.definitionFit: A morsel is a small piece or bite, so a modicum.

clue.text: Old lady can start to say prayer

parts.note: ma is mother, old lady being slang for mother
a tin is a can

indicators.note: start to means the opening letter is taken

explanation.surface: An elderly woman is able to begin saying her prayers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' looks like a verb but is the noun, a tin.
explanation.definitionFit: Matins is the morning service of prayer in the church.

clue.text: Group pleased to accept free gin

indicators.note: accepting means taking the next piece inside

parts.note: content means pleased

indicators.note: set free, the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A party is happy to take free drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' rearranges GIN into ING.
explanation.definitionFit: A contingent is a group of people, such as delegates or troops, forming part of a larger body.

clue.text: Composer being artistic created harmony initially

indicators.note: initially means the opening letters of the words are taken

explanation.surface: A musician, being creative, made a harmony.
explanation.definitionFit: Johann Sebastian Bach was the great German Baroque composer.

clue.text: Supporter first to bring up insult

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: a bra is a supporting garment

indicators.note: first to means the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A backer is the first to bring up a slight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supporter' suggests a fan; it is the undergarment.
explanation.definitionFit: A barb is a cutting remark, so an insult.

clue.text: Suit warms up around summer's end

indicators.note: the warming word goes around the next letter

parts.note: heats means warms up

indicators.note: end means the final letter is taken

explanation.surface: A suit of clothes is warm when summer ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suit' is a card suit, not clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearts is one of the four suits in a pack of playing cards.

clue.text: Beginning to strip, strip off frock

indicators.note: beginning to means the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: to undress is to strip off

explanation.surface: Starting to strip by taking off one's dress.
explanation.definitionFit: A light summer dress with thin straps is a type of frock.
